risks.note: Transformer and wire manufacturing depend on key commodities and industrial raw materials; significant input-price changes can affect margins, particularly where customer contracts lack adequate price-adjustment mechanisms.

The electrical equipment industry is highly competitive and a substantial part of the market operates through tender-based procurement; aggressive competitor pricing may affect order inflows and margins.
Revenue recognition depends on timely execution, inspection, customer clearances and dispatch; delays can shift revenue between financial periods.

The business requires investment in inventories and receivables; the Trade Receivable Turnover Ratio declined from 3.98 to 2.74 and Inventory Turnover declined from 3.86 to 2.54 during the year, indicating slower collections/inventory movement.

Debt Service Coverage Ratio declined from 1.54 to 0.90 during the year, while the Debt Equity Ratio increased from 0.09 to 0.13; management continues to monitor borrowing levels, cash flows and debt-servicing requirements.
Dependence on institutional customers, utilities and tender-driven procurement exposes the Company to fluctuations in order timing, execution schedules and pricing.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
sk.schemes: SECI wind auctions (Tranche-XVII)|GUVNL state wind auctions (Phase X)|Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme|Make in India|Semiconductor initiatives
sk.structure: DG sets classified by capacity: LHP (7.5-160 kVA), MHP (180-500 kVA), HHP (>500 kVA); MSLG sets 3-10 MW for continuous/base-load. Wind potential concentrated in five states: Rajasthan (24%), Gujarat (16%), Maharashtra (15%), Karnataka (15%), Andhra Pradesh (11%).
